name: Statism
summary: Statism holds that the state is legitimate and should be the leading organiser of social and economic life rather than a minimal guard of private property. Its classic thinkers ground this in undivided sovereignty (Bodin, Hobbes) or in the state as the realisation of ethical life (Hegel), and economic statism, as in Kemalist étatisme and French dirigisme, has the state plan, invest, own strategic industries and steer trade and credit while keeping private enterprise. It opposes anarchism, minarchism and laissez-faire, but its adherents divide on democracy, religion and culture.
scope: The state-centred tradition of political thought (Bodin's and Hobbes's sovereignty, Hegel's Philosophy of Right, Fichte's Closed Commercial State) together with twentieth-century economic statism: Kemalist étatisme (RPP programme 1931, 1937 constitution) and post-war French dirigisme under de Gaulle and Pompidou. Gentile's totalitarian 'ethical state' is treated as one pole of the family, not its centre, and full fascism, state socialism, state capitalism and corporatism have their own profiles. Because the family is defined by the scope of state authority, answers on regime form, religion and culture are neutral or low where strands split. No Gaullist primary text could be opened, so the dirigiste strand rests on scholarship.

furtherReading.title: Hobbes's Moral and Political Philosophy (SEP)
furtherReading.note: Clear account of why Hobbes thought sovereign power must be absolute and undivided.

furtherReading.title: Hegel's Social and Political Philosophy (SEP)
furtherReading.note: Introduces Hegel's state, civil society and the debate over whether he was a statist authoritarian.

furtherReading.title: Dirigisme (Wikipedia)
furtherReading.note: Overview of the French model of state-directed capitalism and its spread.

keyFigures.name: Thomas Hobbes
keyFigures.role: Author of Leviathan, the classic argument for an absolute, undivided sovereign.

keyFigures.name: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
keyFigures.role: Philosopher who presented the state as the actuality of ethical life in the Philosophy of Right.

keyFigures.name: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
keyFigures.role: Made statism one of the six founding principles of the Turkish Republic.

sources.title: Leviathan (1651), chs. 18, 19, 21, 29, 30
sources.author: Thomas Hobbes (Project Gutenberg)
sources.usedFor: Sovereign as judge of doctrines and licenser of books; property held from the sovereign; mixed and divided government as diseases; taxes as wages of the public sword; public charity and forced work for the able-bodied; monarchy compared with assemblies; liberty of self-defence.

sources.title: Philosophy of Right (1821), Part III.3: The State
sources.author: G. W. F. Hegel (Marxists Internet Archive, Dyde/Knox translation)
sources.usedFor: State as the actuality of the ethical idea (§§257-261); membership not optional; religion not to govern the state (§270); patriotism (§268); state's own welfare as its highest law abroad and no praetor between states (§§330-337).

sources.title: Philosophy of Right (1821), Part III.2: Civil Society
sources.author: G. W. F. Hegel (Marxists Internet Archive)
sources.usedFor: Public authority's oversight of trade, fixing prices of necessaries, public health, compulsory schooling and vaccination (§§235-239); poverty and the rabble (§§244-245); corporations.

sources.title: Der geschloßne Handelsstaat (The Closed Commercial State, 1800)
sources.author: Johann Gottlieb Fichte (Internet Archive scan)
sources.usedFor: Equal right of all to be able to live from their work; state fixes prices and trades so no one grows very rich or poor; true purpose of the state is not guarding existing heaps of property; the rational state is a closed commercial state, sealed against foreign trade; national money.

sources.title: The Doctrine of Fascism (1932, part I drafted by Giovanni Gentile)
sources.author: Benito Mussolini and Giovanni Gentile (Internet Archive, 1935 official translation)
sources.usedFor: The Gentilean 'ethical state': state absolute, individuals and groups relative; rejection of the night-watchman state, liberalism and class struggle; protection of religion. Used only as the totalitarian pole of the statist family.

sources.title: Hobbes's Moral and Political Philosophy
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Why sovereign powers must be undivided and unlimited; control of doctrine as an essential right; limited rights of resistance; mild pragmatic case for monarchy.

sources.title: Hegel's Social and Political Philosophy
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Constitutional monarchy, estates, corporations, poverty; the debate over whether Hegel was an authoritarian statist.

sources.title: Johann Gottlieb Fichte
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Strong police and welfare functions of the state, duty to manage the economy so every citizen can work, 'communitarian statism', national education.

sources.title: Jean Bodin
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Sovereignty as the highest, absolute and perpetual power, free of positive law; no armed resistance to a sovereign prince.

sources.title: Statism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition and the range of variants (economic statism, state capitalism, corporatism, state nationalism, totalitarian extreme); opposition to anarchism and minarchism.

sources.title: Dirigisme
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: French post-war indicative planning, national champions, state enterprises, technocracy and volontarisme projects (nuclear power), contrast with Soviet planning; Gaullist sponsorship.

sources.title: The 'Little Big Bang' in Paris: financial market deregulation in a dirigiste system
sources.author: Philip G. Cerny, European Journal of Political Research 17(2), 1989 (abstract)
sources.usedFor: Four levels of French dirigisme: planning, a neo-Colbertist civil-service elite, Gaullism and the Fifth Republic, and a state-led credit system as its strategic core.

sources.title: Economic Policies of Kemalism in the Early Republican Era (1923-1938)
sources.author: Tolga Dişçi, BRIq 3(2), 2022
sources.usedFor: Kemalist étatisme: statements by İsmet Pasha and Şeref Bey, state industry office and credit bank, tariffs and exchange controls after 1929, balanced budgets and avoiding external deficits, nationalising railways and ports, land distribution, cooperatives.

sources.title: Nation-Building in China and Turkey: Sun Yat-sen and Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in Comparative Perspective (MA thesis, 2003)
sources.author: Zeyneb Hale Eroğlu, Boğaziçi University
sources.usedFor: Statism as one of the six RPP principles (1931) and in the 1937 constitution; Atatürk's own definitions of statism as planned economy that keeps private enterprise but makes the state responsible for the national economy and industrialisation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Hegel lists the care of public health among the tasks of the public authority (§236 addition) and Hobbes wants the impotent provided for by law; modern statist systems run public health services.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Setting pay by law is a typical interventionist tool, but statism as such has no stated wage policy; inferred from the interventionist variant.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Hegel argues that the large branches of industry need public direction because no individual can grasp the distant conditions they depend on (§236), and İsmet Pasha rejected expecting every blessing from capitalists.

public-ownership.rationale: Kemalist étatisme created state industrial and banking enterprises and nationalised railways, ports and shipping, and French dirigisme kept rail, electricity and gas in state hands, while both left room for private firms.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Statists agree the state should have large revenue, but no source ties statism to soaking the rich; right-leaning dirigiste and corporatist regimes did not.

unions-good.rationale: Corporatist statism incorporates unions into state-controlled bodies while authoritarian variants suppress them, so adherents split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Leviathan ch. 29 calls the doctrine that a subject's property excludes the sovereign's right a cause of dissolution, since property excludes only other subjects; Hegel and the Kemalists still protect private property, so the answer is moderate.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Hegel argues that the more trade sinks into self-seeking the more it needs control from above to bring it back to the universal (§236), and dirigisme steers firms through plans and credit.

cut-welfare.rationale: Hobbes says those unable to work should be provided for by the laws of the commonwealth, and Fichte makes it the state's purpose that all can live; statists back welfare, though tied to work for the able-bodied.

worker-ownership.rationale: Statism places ownership and direction with the state, not with workers; state corporatism organizes workers under state control.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A state with wide legitimate authority and Hobbes's duty to secure peace supports security surveillance; inferred, not stated.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Authoritarian statism favours state enforcement of morality and so would keep drugs illegal, though interventionist statists in liberal states may differ.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The sovereign in Hobbes may restrict speech that threatens peace, and statists accept state regulation of speech; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: A strong executive above party gridlock fits Hobbes's undivided sovereign and the Gaullist Fifth Republic that Cerny counts as a pillar of dirigisme, but Hegel's monarch is closer to a constitutional figurehead, so this rests on the strand.

state-harmful.rationale: Hobbes argues that without a common power men live in a war of all against all, and Hegel calls the state the actuality of ethical life; statism is defined by rejecting the anarchist claim.

limit-guns.rationale: Hobbes gives the state a monopoly of force, and statism favours state control; modern gun policy is inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Hobbes's sovereign exists to secure peace and defense, and strong-state variants emphasise state capacity to enforce order.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Statism has no position; authoritarian variants enforce morality while Nordic-style statists regulate, so split.

decide-locally.rationale: Statism stresses central state authority; Hobbes holds sovereign power indivisible, and French étatisme is centralised.

rehabilitation.rationale: No statist source addresses penal aim; the state's coercive role fits punishment while welfare variants favour rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: Authoritarian statists enforce traditional morality but state feminism and welfare-state variants do not, so adherents differ.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Statism takes no stance; it depends on the regime's culture.

abortion-legal.rationale: No position follows from statism; regimes of both kinds exist.

more-religion-public.rationale: Hobbes subordinates religion to the sovereign rather than banning it, and statism as such is silent, so split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed by statism; active state programmes fit interventionists but not authoritarian nationalists.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A cultural question on which statism is silent.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: State nationalism ties national identity to state authority, so protecting national culture is plausible; liberal civic variants are milder.

gradual-change.rationale: Statism concerns the state's role, not the pace of change; Hobbes dreads upheaval but statist regimes have also imposed rapid change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; state nationalism may favour controls but welfare statists differ.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Hegel dismisses Kant's league of nations as resting on the contingent wills of sovereigns (§333), and sovereignty theory from Bodin onward makes the state the highest power.

free-trade.rationale: Fichte argues that no state that counts on selling abroad can guarantee its subjects' livelihood, and Kemalist policy restricted foreign trade and exchange to build national industry.

nation-first.rationale: Hegel states that a state's highest law in relation to other states is its own welfare and that its wars are justified by its actual interests, not by general philanthropy (§§336-337).

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Hegel rejects universal philanthropy as a ground for a state's action abroad, holding that a state acts on its own interests (§337); statist thought gives no independent warrant for wars to protect foreigners.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders dissolve the state's control over its territory and membership, which is incompatible with state authority; inferred from the core.

limit-growth.rationale: Dirigisme pursued national growth and industrialisation through the state; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Statists favour state action, but statism does not specify environmental priorities.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No stated position; dirigisme funds technology via state R&D but statism is not techno-optimist as such.

expand-nuclear.rationale: French dirigiste volontarisme built a state nuclear power programme as one of its signature projects, the kind of strategic infrastructure statists want the state to drive.

revolution-justified.rationale: Hobbes treats rebellion as dissolving the commonwealth, and statism affirms existing state authority, though state socialism arose through revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Dirigisme rests on a technocratic civil-service elite trained in the grandes écoles, which Cerny calls a neo-Colbertist elite and counts as one of its four pillars.

central-planning.rationale: State socialism holds planning can work, but interventionist and state-capitalist variants keep markets, so statists are genuinely split.

socialized-markets.rationale: Statists accept markets under state ownership or guidance, but the question's worker-or-public condition is only partly theirs.

land-value-tax.rationale: A single land tax is a Georgist proposal; statism favours state revenue broadly but names no particular tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No stated position; revenue-hungry states may favour it, conservative ones not.

basic-income.rationale: Statist thinkers tie support to work: Hobbes would force the able to labour and Hegel treats a claim to subsistence without one's own effort as the mark of the rabble.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: After 1929 the Kemalist government used customs tariffs for its industrialisation drive, and Fichte would close the state to foreign trade altogether; dirigiste France pursued national champions inside a trading bloc.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Directing investment is the defining tool of dirigisme, and Atatürk described statism as making the state responsible for the national economy and for building industry that private activity had not built.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Statism concentrates ownership and direction in the state, not small holders; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Even state socialism keeps wages in practice, and dirigisme depends on markets and profit.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Kemalist leaders said the value of the national currency must not be left to chance outside the government's decisions, and Fichte gives the state sole issue of a national money; leaving money to the market reverses this.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Hegel gives trade corporations a recognised public role in civil society and the Gentilean doctrine builds a corporative state that groups employers and workers under it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Authoritarian and state-socialist variants have one party, but liberal, civic variants have none, so adherents split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hobbes argues monarchy best unites public and private interest (ch. 19) and Hegel defends a hereditary constitutional monarch, but republican étatisme in Turkey and France abolished or rejected monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Statism is defined by the scope of state authority, not its regime: Hobbes prefers monarchy, Hegel a constitutional monarchy, the Gentilean state rejects democracy, while Gaullist and later Kemalist statism worked through elections.

direct-votes.rationale: Undivided central authority in statism sits poorly with plebiscitary rule; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Power in councils instead of the state contradicts the doctrine that state authority is legitimate.

right-to-secede.rationale: Hobbes holds sovereign power cannot be divided and dissolving it dissolves the commonwealth; statism upholds the state's integrity.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; statism rests on legitimacy of the state, not natural hierarchy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Hobbes gives the sovereign the monopoly of force and statist states use violence in defense; adherents do not hold it is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; authoritarian nationalist strands may agree, others not.

separate-church-state.rationale: Statists want the state supreme over religion, but they answer the separation question differently: Hobbes fuses church headship with sovereignty, Kemalism imposed secularism, and the Gentilean state protects Catholicism.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: For Hegel the state is objective, rational law rather than the rule of religious conviction (§270), and Hobbes makes the sovereign, not the clergy, the interpreter of what law binds.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Hobbes annexes judicature and the militia to sovereignty, and the SEP explains his view that adjudication, enforcement and war-making must stay in one undivided power.

military-superiority.rationale: State nationalism and strong-state variants favour state power; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Wikipedia classes state nationalism as civic, tying identity to the state rather than ethnicity, though it can be authoritarian.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism explicitly denies that class struggle is the main factor of history, and Hegel sees history as the unfolding of reason through states.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Fichte's closed state lets no one grow very rich or fall into poverty, but Hegel and the Kemalist and dirigiste states accept unequal private wealth, so the family gives no common answer.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: State authority over all territory is central, so separate authority is disfavoured; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Neither the Wikipedia overview nor Hobbes touches on reparations, so statists have no shared view; it depends on which state is asked to pay.

civilizational-union.rationale: Statism is state-centred, so merging states is disfavoured; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism calls for renouncing self-interest for the state, and Kemalist leaders blamed the Depression on collective interests being run by individual selfishness; Hegel accepts particular interests only when linked to the universal.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Hegel holds that in the state duty and right coincide and that individuals owe duties in proportion to their rights (§261); the Gentilean strand goes further and admits the individual only within the state.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Statism is silent on environmental philosophy; it says who governs, not what has value.

limit-population.rationale: Neither source discusses population policy; statist states have both promoted and limited births, so adherents split.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Dirigisme drove industrialisation, so adherents do not see it as a disaster; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Dirigisme funds technology through state R&D, but speeding change regardless of disruption is not a stated statist aim.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not covered by any statism source; a state with wide authority could either regulate or promote enhancement.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Statism does not discuss algorithms; technocratic planning fits but no source states the position.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A state claiming broad authority resists areas it cannot inspect; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Statism is neither progressive nor restorationist; it is about state authority and spans both reforming and conservative regimes.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Dirigisme is described as not tied to one ideology and pragmatic, but statism itself is a doctrine.

direct-action.rationale: Statism channels change through the state and Hobbes condemns forcing doctrines by arms; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: This is an anarchist-style principle about prefiguration; statism does not address how change methods should resemble the goal.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A state-centred doctrine presupposes organised society and rejects abandoning the state.

distribute-by-need.rationale: State socialism claims need-based distribution as an eventual aim, but interventionist and state-capitalist variants keep market pay, so adherents split.

production-for-use.rationale: State socialist variants hold this; state capitalism and interventionism keep profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Dirigisme keeps private profit and market allocation, so exploitation is not its premise.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Only the state-socialist variant is relevant and statism is not Marxist as such.

collective-farming.rationale: Soviet-type state socialism collectivised farms while dirigiste and corporatist states did not, so statists split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Statist variants include state capitalism and are not committed to this thesis.

taxation-theft.rationale: Leviathan ch. 30 calls taxes the wages owed to those who hold the public sword in defence of everyone's labour, a debt rather than a theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Hobbes regulates opinions for the sake of peace and Hegel's public authority may compel parents to school and vaccinate their children (§239), so state power reaches beyond preventing harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Corporatist statism has individuals owe duty to the state; no group-rights position is stated, so inferred.

conscription.rationale: Hegel's patriotism includes readiness for sacrifice and Kemalist and French states conscripted, but Hobbes lets a subject decline to fight unless he has undertaken it, so the classic texts pull apart.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Statism holds state authority legitimate rather than leaving it as the check; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Statism treats the state as authority, not a firm competing for customers; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Hegel locates substantive freedom in the state and Fichte grounds right in each person's ability to live from work, which points toward material freedom, but the statist family does not state it in these terms.

media-academia-power.rationale: No statist source makes claims about media or universities holding power; it is outside the doctrine.

organic-representation.rationale: State corporatism represents interest groups, but statism spans parliamentary variants too.

total-state.rationale: Wikipedia says totalitarianism favours an all-encompassing state while others favour a small or limited one, so adherents genuinely split.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rebirth narratives belong to fascist and revivalist movements; statism as a general doctrine does not require them.

territorial-expansion.rationale: State nationalism could favour expansion, but Wikipedia describes it as often civic and no statist source endorses conquest generally.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Statism rests on impersonal state authority, not personal fealty; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Hobbes gives the sovereign judgement over doctrine, but statism has no epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: Statism is a doctrine about authority and takes no stand on moral epistemology; Hobbes himself was a relativist or subjectivist about morals.

single-common-good.rationale: Hegel's state realises the universal through particular interests and Gentile's ethical state has a will of its own, which leans toward one common good, though Hegel keeps room for the plural interests of civil society.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Statism concerns how much authority a state has, not which peoples should have one, so it gives no answer on a particular state.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Citizenship for diaspora members is a nationality question; state nationalism may favour it but the sources state no position.

revive-national-language.rationale: State nationalism could favour it but no source says so.

workplace-democracy.rationale: State direction of firms replaces democratic control; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: State-run provision is favoured over private choice by statists; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Kemalist étatisme insisted on balanced budgets while investing through state enterprises, but later dirigiste and welfare statists used deficits, so no single answer follows.

economic-freedom.rationale: Hegel says freedom of trade must not endanger the general good and needs control from above (§236), and statists hold that political order rests on the state rather than on economic liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Statism relies on state law and enforcement; Hobbes stresses sovereign force and law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed; state nationalism ties nation to state.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; sovereigntist inclination offset by variety.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Hobbes grounds the state in reasoning about peace yet lets the sovereign regulate religion, and statism takes no general stand on reason against faith.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; welfare-state variants disagree among themselves.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Hobbes writes that those with strong bodies are to be forced to work, with laws encouraging trades so none can plead lack of employment, and Hegel warns of a rabble claiming subsistence as a right without work.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects class struggle in favour of unity within the state, and Hegel's state stands above the particular interests of civil society as their universal; the state arbitrates between classes rather than serving one.

dominated-front.rationale: Dirigiste Asian and Indian states did pursue autonomy from the West, but statism as such has no stated foreign alignment.

workers-nation.rationale: Whether workers organise nationally or internationally is a socialist dispute; statist variants differ by regime.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Authoritarian variants enforce traditional morality, but state feminism exists too.

ban-interest.rationale: Dirigisme runs through state-guided investment and credit, not interest bans; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not a statist position; civic state nationalism is listed instead.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Statism treats the state as the universal standing above particular interests: Hegel's state is the actuality of the ethical idea and Gentile's ethical state amalgamates classes, the reverse of the Marxist view.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy choice is not part of statism; dirigiste states have directed both fossil and nuclear development.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: State nationalism could favour it, but no source says so.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claim not tied to statism.

proportional-representation.rationale: Hobbes is indifferent to the form of the sovereign, and statism takes no position on electoral systems.

national-mission.rationale: A mission to spread one's government is a nationalist or imperial idea; statism does not mandate it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Wikipedia notes state feminism in both liberal and authoritarian forms, so statists disagree about whether the state should challenge patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Statism defends state authority as legitimate, which sits badly with a blanket charge that rulers are corrupt, though reformers inside it may make it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Statism affirms state authority and does not address prosecuting past abuses; adherents of liberal and authoritarian variants would differ.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The 1932 Doctrine of Fascism says outright that the state is 'not a night watchman', and Fichte writes that the state's true purpose is not to guard existing heaps of property; dirigiste and Kemalist statism likewise give the state an economic role.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Hobbes starts from the natural equality of men and Hegel from universal personhood, but the Gentilean state values individuals only within the state, so the answer is guarded.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Only relevant to the state-socialist strand.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Whether settler states are colonial projects is a historical dispute that statism as a doctrine does not address.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Statists want one law for all subjects from one sovereign, and Kemalism made secular nationhood a founding principle, though the sources here do not discuss a civil code.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Authoritarian variants that enforce a state religion might, but statism has no stated policy on conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious-cultural policy that depends on the regime, not on the statist doctrine itself.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Hobbes lets the sovereign decide which doctrines are taught, so no fixed answer follows for religion in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Stalinist argument inside state socialism, one strand of statism, and other strands do not share it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Hobbes bases sovereignty on covenant, but statism requires legitimacy only to some degree and includes authoritarian forms.

trade-surplus.rationale: Kemalist policy explicitly aimed at avoiding external deficits through trade and exchange controls, and Fichte sought to keep a closed state independent of foreign money.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Coercion by the sovereign, from taxation to compulsory schooling, is the means statist thinkers rely on, so a ban on initiating force rules out the state they defend.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Statism favours directed cooperation under the state, as in corporatism.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: A state that claims broad authority may protect its order; Hobbes lets the sovereign suppress seditious doctrines.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: This republican idea of freedom is not part of statism; Hobbes in fact rejects it in favour of freedom as absence of impediment.

separated-powers.rationale: Hobbes and Bodin hold that sovereign power must be undivided and that dividing it dissolves the state; the dirigiste and Kemalist republics kept distinct branches but concentrated direction in the executive, so the answer is disagree rather than strong.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist idea that belongs only to the state-socialist strand of statism, not to the general doctrine.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Welfare-state statists may accept it while state-capitalist and authoritarian variants prioritise national strength, so it splits them.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Selling public housing to tenants is a market-oriented policy that welfare statists oppose and some conservative statists support.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Corporatist states channelled labour into state bodies, but welfare variants do not.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Statism sees poverty as a matter for state action and takes no stand on Malthusian causes.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: State nationalism may emphasise cohesion, but Wikipedia describes it as civic, so no stated answer on diversity.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Hobbes's sovereign decides what keeps peace; inferred for statism.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Hegel says the public authority may fix the prices of the commonest necessaries of life, since goods in universal daily demand are offered to the public as a whole (§236); Fichte has the state fix prices by law.

party-controls-media.rationale: Hobbes makes the sovereign the judge of which doctrines may be taught and gives it the right to examine books before publication (ch. 18); modern statists differ on how far this extends to news, which keeps it at agree.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the army is found in Soviet-type state socialism but not in other statist regimes, so adherents split.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship rules are not defined by statism; state nationalists might prefer long waits, welfare statists less so.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: This is a Marxist and Paris Commune demand; statism has no position on pay of officials.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding party discipline is a Leninist rule specific to some state-socialist variants, not a general statist position.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Bodin and Hobbes define sovereignty as the highest power that cannot be shared without being lost, which tells against pooling it in a supranational body.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Hobbes allows monarch or assembly; statism spans both.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Hobbes puts church government under the civil sovereign, but statism has no doctrine on episcopal versus congregational forms.

clerical-rule.rationale: Hegel writes that religion must not govern the state, since that makes subjective feeling the lawgiver and leads to fanaticism (§270), and Hobbes counts 'pretence of inspiration' among the causes of dissolution.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Statism affirms state authority and national interest in war, the opposite of revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Authoritarian variants enforce morality; others not.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are a constitutional detail on which Hobbes's indifference to the form of sovereign leaves statism neutral.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is a democratic mechanism; liberal statists may accept it and strong-sovereign variants reject it.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Statism does not address alliances; strong-state nationalists could prefer autonomy but dirigiste Asian states relied on alliances.

people-in-arms.rationale: Hobbes and statism favour the state's monopoly of force over armed citizens; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Dirigisme drove urban industrialisation, but statism makes no moral claim about rural or urban life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: State nationalism ties nation to state, which might favour reunification, but no source states this view.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: This populist claim is not part of statism, which often relies on educated technocrats and planners.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not a statist doctrine; state nationalism may prize one national culture, but no common stance exists.

death-penalty.rationale: Hobbes's sovereign holds the power to punish, and strong-state variants accept it; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The curriculum depends on the regime's values; state feminism in welfare states would support it and moralist authoritarian states not.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Statism has no stance on science teaching; Hobbes lets the sovereign set what is taught, which could go either way.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: State nationalism may prefer descent or territory, and Wikipedia describes it as civic, so statism gives no fixed answer.

minority-language-support.rationale: State nationalism may favour one language, but no source says so.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Hegel holds that the state must uphold its objective law against claims grounded only in subjective conviction (§270), so religious belief does not exempt anyone from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not a statist concern; inferred from state-enforced morality in authoritarian variants.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Statism upholds state authority but has no view on debt between states; creditor and debtor states would answer oppositely.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Post-independence India and others did link independence to state-led economic change under dirigisme, but this is not stated as a general principle.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Hobbes treats any sovereign as legitimate once established, and statism takes no stand on how constitutions are written.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Kemalist étatisme pursued rapid state-led development under one-party rule, but French dirigisme ran inside a democracy, so the link is not a statist principle.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Statism concerns domestic state authority and gives no verdict on international aid duties.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Strong-state and state-nationalist variants favour national capability, as in dirigiste France; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Statism is indifferent to how the head of state is chosen, as Hobbes allows a monarch or an assembly.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Statist practice treats money and credit as instruments of state policy, from Kemalist currency control to the French state-led credit system, rather than as a technocratic domain walled off from government.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions are a foreign policy matter on which statism, a doctrine about state authority, takes no side.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Fichte says each should hold what is his by right rather than what luck or force brought him, and Hobbes holds property from the sovereign for the sake of peace; ownership answers to the public end.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: State socialism and state capitalism are both statist variants and the label is contested.

precautionary-principle.rationale: State regulation to prevent harm fits statism; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Statism does not address alliance treaties; sovereigntist states may reject them while others join pacts.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Statism does not decide the status of annexed territory; state nationalism and international law pull in different directions.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Hobbes makes the Christian sovereign head of the church in his dominions with the right to appoint pastors, Hegel has the state uphold rational law against church claims, and Kemalism placed religion under state control; Gentile's state instead protects the Church.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Statism says nothing about the form of head of state; variants run from monarchy to party leadership.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Undivided sovereignty and territorial authority of the state imply defending its integrity; inferred from Hobbes and the state-centred view.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Indivisible sovereignty and state-directed economies lean toward one legal and economic system; inferred, as statism has no stated autonomy doctrine.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Hobbes's sovereign rests on contract and not on divine descent, and modern statism is secular; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Interventionist states use progressive taxation to fund and steer the economy; inferred from the dirigiste variant.

character-from-environment.rationale: Statism has no doctrine of human nature across its variants, from Hobbes's fixed nature to state-socialist environmentalism.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Hobbes calls the opinion that the sovereign is subject to the civil laws a doctrine repugnant to the commonwealth, and Bodin frees the sovereign from positive law; later constitutional statists bind rulers to a constitution, which tempers the answer.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; state-led space programmes fit dirigisme but statism does not make expansion a central goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Leviathan ch. 29 lists 'mixt government' among the diseases of a commonwealth, since mixing king, lords and commons sets three sovereigns against one another.

leader-cult.rationale: Some statist regimes cultivate leader cults while others do not; the doctrine itself is silent.

equal-parenting.rationale: No statist position on custody law; neutral inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred: statism holds the state's authority is legitimate and stands above class, so continuing class struggle is not its framing.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Kemalist government seized large estates in some regions and gave them to landless peasants, but this is one case rather than a doctrine of the statist family.

refugee-return.rationale: Statism does not address refugee return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Statism does not address irredentism; variants split.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Hobbes gives the sovereign the right to judge doctrines, but statism as such has no stated position on apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred: statism is silent on dress, though liberal-welfare variants would oppose it.

common-currency.rationale: Statism does not address monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Statism does not address pan-national unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from Hobbes' undivided sovereignty, which resists separate institutions within the state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Statism has no stated theory of historical change.

ban-cartels.rationale: Dirigiste states both break up and build national champions; no stated position.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from dirigisme, where state-owned and guided firms are rescued by the state.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Hobbes places the sovereign beyond check, but statism does not equate it with majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Statism has no stated position on gender quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Fichte's closed commercial state is autarkic, but it has no colonies and later statists traded openly, so a colonial trading bloc is only loosely implied.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Statism has no stated position on trade conditions.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: statist economies rely on law, ownership and material incentives rather than moral exhortation.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Hobbes' sovereign is undivided and subjects have a very limited right to resist, so rebels are condemned.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Statism does not address hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Statism includes state nationalism, which favours a national-centred curriculum; inferred, as the sources give no education policy.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Statism has no stated position on imperial rule; its variants split.

patriotic-education.rationale: Hobbes wants the people instructed in their duties through schools, universities and set days, Hegel's state may compel schooling, and Fichte's Addresses centre on national education.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Statism as such has no stated view; its variants split.

public-money-creation.rationale: A state that directs investment and the economy can reasonably control money creation; inferred from dirigisme.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Dirigiste state guidance is meant to steer capitalism through crises; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: No source addresses former empires; the variants split.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dirigisme uses tariffs and state enterprise but still trades in the world market; adherents are split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Statism stresses state authority over class or global divisions; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Statism rejects minimal-state theory and accepts state limits on private conduct; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Hobbes holds that sovereign power is undivided and cannot be bound, which conflicts with entrenched limits; inferred for the family.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from Hobbes's view that covenants bind and from the continuity of state authority.

elective-rulers.rationale: Statism covers states of every constitutional form, and Hobbes allows sovereignty in a monarch or an assembly, so adherents split on election.

minority-veto.rationale: Hobbes's undivided sovereignty means the sovereign's decisions bind all subjects, and a dissenter cannot hold a veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Hobbes allows subjects only to defend their own bodies, and Bodin forbids taking up arms against a sovereign prince even when tyrannical; the classic statist position denies a general right to depose rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Hobbes places sovereignty in either a monarch or an assembly, so adherents are split on whether Parliament must be supreme.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from a general modern moral view; statism takes no firm position, so this is a weak inference.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred as for the previous statement: a state-regulating outlook accepts humane limits on use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from a state taking a leading part in social life, which welfare provision expresses.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred from the claim that political authority is legitimate and civic life is under the state's care, not apart from it.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from the strand's lack of any theory of culture as domination.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hobbes holds that governing men's opinions is how actions are governed, which resembles rule by consent through culture, but statists do not frame this as a ruling class.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from dirigisme's market-and-trade orientation, which does not hold that poverty is structurally extracted.

native-born-offices.rationale: State nationalist variants favour it and liberal-dirigiste variants do not, so adherents are split.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from the stress on state sovereignty and authority over foreign direction.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Kemalist policy refused to close budget gaps with foreign debt and aimed at national capital accumulation, reacting against Ottoman dependence on foreign creditors.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchist state nationalists favour it and other statists do not, so adherents are split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from a state that governs all citizens under one authority, which resists rule by descent.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Statism includes both fascist and democratic state forms, so adherents are split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Statism includes both fascist and communist state forms, so adherents are split on condemning them together.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream historical view that the strand does not contest.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The strand takes no position on historical symbols and adherents are split.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from a state that takes a leading part in social programmes for all groups.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the state's role in protecting all subjects equally.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the view that the state need not follow one model and may take varied forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Statism covers both civilian and military-led states, so adherents are split.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from a state-led social role that funds care provision.

filial-duty.rationale: Statism is a family of views and gives no stance on family duties; adherents are split.

office-by-exam.rationale: French dirigisme recruited its administrators through elite competitive schools, but the classic statist texts say little about how offices are filled.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Kemalist Turkey turned railways and ports formerly held by Western interests into national property, and dirigiste France protected strategic sectors as national champions.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Statist strands split on social questions such as divorce law; the doctrine is silent.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Hobbes's case for indivisible sovereign authority tells against mandates binding rulers, though liberal welfare-state strands would differ; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Statism favours a major state role in providing social security, so private individual accounts are inferred as disfavoured, though strands vary.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Hobbes has property held from the sovereign, but statist strands range from state ownership to private holding, so they are split.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The liberal welfare-state strand favours legislative budget control while the authoritarian strand does not, so adherents are split.

single-official-language.rationale: Statist strands split on language and culture policy; the doctrine is silent.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Statist strands split on land and foreign ownership; the doctrine is silent.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Statist strands split on anti-discrimination law; the doctrine is silent.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Statist strands split on consumer culture, from welfare states to state-socialist asceticism; the doctrine is silent.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Statist strands split on covert and foreign policy; the doctrine is silent.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Statist strands split on alliance intervention; the doctrine is silent.

corporate-influence.rationale: State-capitalist strands fuse state and business while interventionist ones restrain it; adherents split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: A state claiming authority over national life would readily control foreign funding; inferred from the sovereignty emphasis.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Statism has no stated population policy; adherents vary.

residents-only-property.rationale: Undivided sovereignty and central direction run against local authorities restricting property; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Fichte holds that all have an equal right to be able to live from their work and that the state must arrange trades so this holds, and the SEP notes his state's duty to ensure every citizen can employ their labour.

democratic-peace.rationale: Statism has no stated view of democracy and peace; strands differ on regime form.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Hobbes names the doctrine that every private man is judge of good and evil as a cause of dissolution, and Hegel calls membership of the state the individual's highest duty (§258).

non-intervention.rationale: Hobbes treats sovereigns as in a state of nature with each other, and strands differ; no stated position.

industrial-unions.rationale: No source gives a statist view on union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not a statist doctrine; strands focused on state authority would reject minority conspiracy claims; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Hobbes treats marriage as governed by civil law and the state regulates it; inferred opposition to abolition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Hobbes gives the sovereign the right to judge doctrines and control information; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Dirigisme uses tariffs and national industry but no source addresses local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Statism rejects anarchism and stateless organisation, and favours permanent state institutions.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Hegel says international law remains an 'ought' without enforcement, that states stay in a state of nature towards one another, and that there is no praetor to judge between states (§§330-333).

religious-nation.rationale: Statism has no stated position on religion; strands differ.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Statism as a family has no stated doctrine on tribute or hierarchy among states; adherents are split.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Statism favours central authority and state-led distribution, so regional retention is inferred as opposed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: State socialist strands hold means of production in common while state capitalist ones do not; the family is split.

defeat-communism.rationale: Strands range from anti-communist state nationalism to state socialism; adherents are split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Dirigisme uses state-owned and private firms alike, but state socialism wants direct delivery; split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Statism is not tied to any view on religion; strands range from secular to religious.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Strands are split on whether capitalism was a progressive stage.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: No unified position; state socialist strands link equality to economic change while others do not.

socialized-care.rationale: State-provided services fit the interventionist strands, but the family is split on private roles.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language policy is not part of the doctrine; adherents are split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Hobbes's case for undivided sovereign authority implies the state cannot be bound by outside parties; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Statism holds the state's authority legitimate and central, which conflicts with self-governing communities replacing it.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settlement policy varies across strands; adherents are split.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Dirigisme is described as a middle way between American state minimalism and Soviet total control, Kemalist étatisme kept private enterprise under state direction, and the Gentilean doctrine rejects both liberalism and socialism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Statism is not a territorial doctrine and its strands split on nationalism; neutral inference.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; no strand of statism rests on denial, so inferred as strong disagreement.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Statism spans liberal welfare states and authoritarian regimes, so it takes no common line; leaning against as an inference from modern statist states.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Statist strands split between democratic welfare states and authoritarian regimes, so adherents disagree.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Hobbes let the sovereign judge doctrines, but modern statist strands disagree; split.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; strands range from imperial to anti-colonial states.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Unrelated to statism; no basis to infer a position.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Hobbes held that subjects have only a limited right to resist the sovereign, which counts against removing rulers by force.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Statism stresses central authority and officials directing society, so direct participation is a secondary value; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Statist strands are split on cultural and identity questions.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Statist strands are split on this cultural question.

assisted-dying.rationale: Statist strands are split; the doctrine does not address it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Statism spans left and right variants and takes no stance on the divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: State socialist strands accept this idea while state capitalist and dirigiste strands reject it.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; strands are split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Hobbes grounded sovereign authority in a covenant among people, not directly in God, and most statism is secular; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Statist strands are split; some favour secular state institutions and others do not.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from statism's acceptance of state regulation of employment and markets; the sources do not address it.

social-market-economy.rationale: Statism rejects laissez-faire but also includes a larger state role than this statement allows, as in state capitalism and state socialism, so adherents are split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Statism treats the state's authority as legitimate, and Hobbes made the sovereign's power to protect the core of the state; abolishing its armed forces contradicts this.

rich-first.rationale: Dirigiste strands used state-directed uneven growth while state socialist strands reject it; split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Statist states have taken both aligned and non-aligned courses; split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Statism spans monarchies to republics; Hobbes allowed the sovereign to choose a successor but the family is not committed on it.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Statism favours state-directed credit and banks rather than user-owned mutual banks; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Dirigisme asserts the state's economic autonomy; refusing lender-imposed conditions is inferred to fit, though not stated.

property-franchise.rationale: Statism does not require a restricted franchise and the family splits on democracy; a property qualification is inferred to be disfavoured.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Statism is silent on this ecofeminist claim; adherents are split.

reification.rationale: Statists accept state-led capitalism or socialism but not this critique as core; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Statists are split between those who would regulate media ownership and those who would use the state to control the press.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Hegel insists that laws must be made universally known to bind (§215), and Hobbes says the sovereign governs through declared civil laws; Bodin's sovereign also rules by law, though free to change it.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial restriction of the franchise is not part of the statist core and is inferred to be rejected.

online-participation.rationale: The family says little about participation channels; adherents are split.

open-government-data.rationale: The family is split between transparent administration and secrecy of the state.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Statism says nothing on marriage law; adherents are split by culture.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: A consumer boycott of a minority is not a statist position and is inferred to be disfavoured.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Statism stresses the state's authority to decide, so binding lot-chosen assemblies sit uneasily with it, though some variants are democratic; inferred from the definition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Hobbes has the sovereign judge religious doctrine, which could mean either reform or enforcement, and statism as such takes no side; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Statists split on whether to curb large fortunes; dirigisme may do so but the doctrine does not require it; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The doctrine is silent on this and statists range from conservative to progressive; inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Hobbes lets the sovereign set public religion but treats atheism as a threat to obedience, so promoting unbelief is not part of the doctrine; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Statism is defined against anarchism and minimal-state theory, and an authoritative state needs police and coercive enforcement.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Hobbes argues that sovereign power must be undivided, which cuts against guaranteed shares of executive power for communities; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Leviathan ch. 30 says those disabled by unavoidable accident ought not be left to the charity of private persons but provided for by the laws, since exposing them to uncertain charity is uncharitable in a sovereign.

term-limits.rationale: Nothing in the doctrine bears on term limits and adherents split by regime type; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Delegable voting spreads authority away from the sovereign and the state's institutions; inferred from the case for undivided authority.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: A state with a leading role in directing society is a natural body to coordinate large-scale risk prevention; inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The doctrine is silent on religious office and adherents split on gender equality; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The doctrine is silent on household authority and adherents split between traditional and egalitarian views; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Statism is a broad orientation; democratic variants might extend local votes while nation-state variants would not, so no common view.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: a state that intervenes in economic and social life readily regulates prices, as dirigisme does, but statist variants differ.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: state-directed investment and state-owned enterprise rely on state-protected property rights over innovation, though no source addresses it.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Statist regimes have used youth organisations, but the broad doctrine is split and does not require them.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Statism says nothing on where nuclear weapons are based; sovereign-state authority fits either answer.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on undivided sovereign authority within a territory, which tells against foreign forces on it.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The doctrine gives no position on recognising past killings; statist states vary in whether they do.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: State socialist variants favour reward for work, while state capitalist ones accept returns on ownership; adherents split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Hobbes, the classical case, grounds the state in the right of self-preservation, which includes self-defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Statism covers state nationalism and non-national forms alike, so it takes no stated view on national continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Statism is not a theory of sex or gender; adherents are split along other lines.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Statism has no position on feminist theory; adherents are split.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: State-nationalist variants honour fallen soldiers while others do not; the broad doctrine is neutral.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Hobbes's case for the state is secular and about peace and security, not a spiritual battle of good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Statism says nothing about diasporas, and state-nationalist variants differ.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: statism puts political authority and state-building first, so it would not wait on cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Statism has no theology; Hobbes treats religion as subject to the sovereign, with no view on divine gender.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Statism is not tied to any religious view, and the sources do not address it.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: State capitalism in nation-states may favour national ownership, but the broad doctrine does not require it.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: State-nationalist variants might merge regions, but the broad doctrine has no stated territorial position.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred: statism puts organisations under state authority and direction, so union independence from the state is not a core value, though variants differ.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: statism centres on state authority rather than working-class rule, so adherents would not make workers' power a test of socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Wikipedia's account of economic statism includes state ownership of enterprises and services, which fits keeping local essentials public.

second-chamber.rationale: Statism says little about legislative form; Hobbes favoured undivided sovereignty, but statist states use both unicameral and bicameral systems.

municipal-property.rationale: Statism places ownership and direction in the state; community ownership outside state control contradicts that.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Statism upholds the state's undivided authority, and Hobbes argued sovereignty cannot be divided, so assemblies keeping decisions against a coordinating centre run against it.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; statist variants range from welfare states to state capitalism, with no common wage position.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; state regulation of medicine is accepted but speed is not a statist concern.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; a state directing investment could fund it, but it is not a statist doctrine.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: a state claiming leading economic authority will want to trace and control money flows, as dirigisme steers finance.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred: statism favours state authority and oversight, which is in tension with anonymity from the state.

person-over-state.rationale: Hegel rejects the view that the state exists only to secure individuals' property and freedom (§258), and the Doctrine of Fascism calls the state absolute and individuals relative, though Hegel also insists the state must satisfy its members' subjective ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not addressed; statism is neutral on religion, and adherents range from secular to confessional states.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Statism holds that the central state is the source of authority, so regional powers are delegated and revocable; Hobbes's sovereign is undivided.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; a dirigiste state could promote it but the doctrine says nothing on it.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; state planning could favour density, but this is not a statist position.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: statism rests on the state's authority over all subjects rather than on racial groups, though state-nationalist variants may differ.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; statism is neutral on this and its variants differ.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed; statism covers both pacific and militarist states, and Hobbes's sovereign decides on war.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Statism is not a nation-defining doctrine; adherents differ.

communal-electorates.rationale: No stated position; state nationalists reject it while others are indifferent.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not part of the general doctrine; varies by variant.

free-public-college.rationale: A state taking a leading part in social life readily funds higher education, but statism sets no policy on tuition; inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Statists could use taxes or direct regulation; the doctrine does not choose.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred indifference.

arms-reduction.rationale: Hobbes's sovereign needs strength to secure peace and protection, so adherents lean against disarmament; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: In Hobbes the sovereign alone judges foreign relations and negotiation, so confidential dealing is accepted; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Kemalist Turkey imposed foreign exchange control by the 1930 law protecting the currency, and French dirigisme rested on a state-led credit system that steered industrial finance.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Hobbes annexes the militia and the right of war to the sovereign alone, and the SEP notes that splitting force from the other sovereign powers invites civil war.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Hegel's patriotism demands readiness to sacrifice, yet Hobbes concedes a subject may decline to fight unless he undertook it, so the classic sources pull apart.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Dirigiste and corporatist variants may favour union bargaining while others prefer state-set terms; inferred from the split in the variants.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: A state that guides the economy readily supplements incomes; inferred from Wikipedia's treatment of welfare as a statist form.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Statism favours state discretion over the economy, so fixed legal limits on borrowing sit badly with it; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Statism says little on global economic rules; state-led development fits reform, state-capitalist variants may favour the existing order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Statism holds the state is legitimate and to be used, in contrast to anarchism, which seeks to abolish it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Dirigisme works through state planning and guided investment rather than leaving systems open; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: State-guided investment and planning extend readily to treating natural resources as managed assets; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Hegel calls the state the divine will present in the world and the Gentilean doctrine treats it as a spiritual entity outliving individuals, but statism centres the state rather than the nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Statism does not address student loans; adherents split between state generosity and fiscal discipline.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Statism treats the state as a unifying authority and does not speak of regional exploitation; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Hobbes grounds the state in natural equality and fear, but statism takes no stand on a sacred human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: State-run broadcasters fit the interventionist mixed economy, though independence from the state is not a statist aim; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Statism is not a religious doctrine, so this is left neutral; the profile's scope says religion answers are mostly neutral.

farm-price-support.rationale: Kemalist policy set up agricultural cooperatives and used the state agricultural bank to shield farmers from merchants who drove crop prices down.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on undivided sovereign authority and security (Hobbes); a statist state keeps the means of its own defence.

workers-own-party.rationale: Statist variants split: state socialism backs labour parties, while state-nationalist and corporatist forms oppose independent class parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the view that the state may legislate in social life and that sovereign law binds all subjects.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the statist view that law should apply uniformly, and from mainstream modern statist states' equal-rights law; variants differ.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Naming of languages is a cultural question statism does not settle.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Statists prefer state agencies and regulation to a tort-only regime, which minarchist theory favours; inferred from the rejection of minimal-state theory.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Hobbes's indivisible sovereignty leaves no room for a separate official body with a lawmaking role; inferred from that principle.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: A state that takes a leading part in economic and social life readily subordinates individual liberty to collective goals like the environment; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Fixed penalties express the sovereign's authority over the judiciary; inferred from the strong-state emphasis.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from state nationalism and the sovereign's right to set conditions for subjects; variants differ.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Statism is a broad family and does not address union membership; adherents split between dirigiste and market-friendly forms.

voter-id.rationale: Statism says nothing specific on voter identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Hobbes's view that the sovereign judges which doctrines are taught, which favours a state-ranked religion; adherents vary.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Statists split on democracy, and the stress on undivided sovereign authority over procedure leans against a purely procedural test.

premarital-sex.rationale: Statism is silent on sexual morality; adherents are split.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the stress on state authority and order, which supports emergency powers; internet access is anachronistic for classical statism.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from dirigiste support for state-run programmes, which runs against replacing welfare with cash payments.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the general view that the state may grant equal rights; statism itself is silent and adherents are split.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Statism does not address religion's role in women's oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Statism does not address the nature of racial categories.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Statism is indifferent to whether the state should create gender equality agencies; adherents vary.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Hobbes holds that property is held from the sovereign, and economic statism puts resources under state direction, not first-claim ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the indivisible sovereignty of the state, which sits uneasily with courts above the nation.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Statism has no doctrine on scripture; Hobbes gave the sovereign the right to judge doctrines.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Statism as a broad orientation takes no stated position on gender in self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from state ownership and planning being among statism's forms, though variants differ on defending a bureaucratic state.

indirect-election.rationale: Statism takes no position on how higher offices are filled; its variants include democratic and authoritarian forms.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from Hobbes, who has the sovereign set public worship, so a state church above others fits the doctrine.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of undivided sovereign authority, which resists dividing power by territory.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: Hobbes holds that the sovereign, not a local vote, decides, though other variants are split.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from respect for established state authority and its settled jurisdiction.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: a state directing the economy aims at growth and provision, not minimal needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Statism has no stated position on indigenous settlement; adherents are split.

equal-conscription.rationale: Statism accepts state power to conscript but says nothing on sex equality in the draft; adherents are split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The statist sources say nothing on this, and the scope of state authority does not settle it either way.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Statist thinkers want order through the state's own courts and laws: Hegel stresses public courts and known law, so killing without trial undermines the legal state, though none addresses this case.

close-ties-china.rationale: The statist sources say nothing on this, and the scope of state authority does not settle it either way.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The statist sources say nothing on this, and the scope of state authority does not settle it either way.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The statist sources say nothing on this, and the scope of state authority does not settle it either way.

self-ownership.rationale: Hobbes keeps a right to defend one's body but makes property and labour's fruits depend on the sovereign, and Fichte has the state allocate trades, so full self-ownership cuts against the tradition, though no statist text uses the term.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Hobbes argues that taxes are most equal when laid on what people consume, but later statists rely on many kinds of taxes, so this rests on one thinker.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The statist sources say nothing on this, and the scope of state authority does not settle it either way.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Hobbes counts factions and subordinate bodies as dangers to the sovereign but Hegel builds representation through estates and corporations, so the strands differ.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The statist sources say nothing on this, and the scope of state authority does not settle it either way.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Hegel keeps religion from governing the state and Kemalism made secularism a founding principle, which points against politics organised by denomination.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The statist sources say nothing on this, and the scope of state authority does not settle it either way.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The statist sources say nothing on this, and the scope of state authority does not settle it either way.

national-resource-control.rationale: The Kemalist state took over mines, railways and ports from foreign control as a national question, and the state-owned strategic sectors of dirigisme serve the same goal.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Statism holds that the state organises economic life, and Hegel's civil society needs public regulation, so outcomes can be judged and corrected; inferred from that.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Interventionist statism, such as dirigisme, steers credit and finance, so taxing financial flows fits; inferred, not stated.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Statism says nothing on racial advancement; its adherents divide on culture and society.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Hobbes holds that the sovereign is the source of law and that subjects are bound by it, and Hegel grounds right in the state; unjust law still binds.

automate-paid-work.rationale: No stated position; state planning may favour automation but strands differ on work and employment, so inferred neutral.

multipolar-world.rationale: Statists agree on strong sovereignty but split on world order; Gaullist dirigisme favoured multipolarity while others favoured a strong dominant state; inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Statism's classic thinkers and economic statists do not rest on a labour theory of value; inferred from their state-centred and mixed-economy views.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Statists split between nationalist strands that tie state and people together and others with no stated link; inferred neutral.

material-over-identity.rationale: Adherents divide on culture; the family is defined by state authority, not by left priorities; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Statism favours state leadership of the economy, but is not defined by communist rule, and Kemalist and dirigiste strands were not communist; inferred.

notes: Re-audit of a thin earlier profile. Strands that would answer differently: Gentile's ethical state (total-state, suppress-opposition, war near +2), Fichte's closed commercial state (central-planning, free-trade, equal-outcomes strongly statist), and democratic dirigisme (democracy-best and civil liberties positive). Unrevised answers carried over from the earlier audit remain low confidence.
